java_locations.role: With a single requested family, always derives that primary Java AWT Font; any physical-glyph fallback remains AWT Font behavior rather than selecting a different PlantUML family.
Returns the face-aware AWT Font used for the complete text.
Measures that AWT Font with fractional FontMetrics.getStringBounds.
Uses the same resolved font for layout dimensions and descent.

rust_locations.role: Uses exact four-face tables only for printable ASCII and assigns every other scalar 1024 units.
The checked-in derivation currently emits only printable ASCII even though the same AWT API can derive assigned Unicode scalar advances.

claimed_invariant: For text whose AWT width is scalar-additive, every assigned Unicode scalar is measured with the same Times New Roman face and JDK fallback behavior as printable ASCII, scaled to the requested size as f32, and accumulated in source order as f32. Plain, bold, italic, and bold-italic layout widths therefore reproduce the same additive AWT path that SVG emission names.
causal_divergence: The original implementation deliberately replaced every non-ASCII scalar with a half-em advance. The first Unicode-table correction then rounded every AWT advance independently to an integer at a 2048-point extraction size. Java retains 16 fractional bits in these measurements and sums those fractional scalar advances before scaling. For additive scripts, repeated fractional-width scalars such as U+0518 therefore accumulate a visible width error even though the selected face and codepoint coverage are correct.

derivation.domain: Every Character.isDefined Unicode scalar in the pinned JDK, excluding surrogate code points, for all four binary faces.
derivation.encoding: Unsigned 16.16 fixed-point advances at a 2048-point extraction size, stored as u32 tuples and compressed into maximal consecutive codepoint ranges sharing the same four-face tuple; undefined scalars use a separately extracted missing-glyph tuple.

preimplementation_probe.fixed_point_fit: The maximum observed 16.16 value is below u32::MAX.
preimplementation_probe.awt_accumulation_probe: For 32 repetitions of U+0518, scaling the exact 2048-point advance to sizes 17 and 19 as f32 and accumulating as f32 exactly equals Font.getStringBounds on the complete string: 560.864135742188 and 626.847839355469.

planned_model_change: Change the checked-in Java extractor and generated Rust range table from rounded u16 design units to exact u32 16.16 fixed-point advances, with a generation-time assertion that every AWT width is represented exactly and fits u32. For strings containing non-ASCII scalars, binary-search the same ranges, convert both Unicode and printable-ASCII advances to the requested size as f32, and accumulate in source order as f32 before returning f64, matching AWT's additive glyph-position path. Preserve the established all-ASCII f64 path and cross-check the overlapping arrays. Do not add string-specific values, script guesses, state offsets, or route changes.
scope_residue: This mechanism corrects additive scalar advances. Contextual shaping, ligatures, grapheme clusters, emoji sequences, and font-stack definitions containing multiple comma-separated families are not claimed to be solved by a scalar table and remain separate mechanisms. The checker must distinguish an additive-advance failure from that declared shaping residue.
perturbation_axes: Latin-1 accents versus ASCII base letters
plain versus bold versus italic versus bold-italic
state titles and attributes versus ordinary and self transition labels
repetition counts that accumulate fractional scalar advances
precomposed characters versus combining marks as a residue probe
acceptance: Both preserved Unicode counterexamples have exact additive text metrics and are structurally equivalent unless an independently identified out-of-scope residue remains.
Fresh valid additive-script perturbations across all four faces match Java without per-input constants.
The checked-in extractor deterministically regenerates the range table and verifies the original printable-ASCII arrays.
The full renderer library suite passes.
The no-oracle product gate does not regress any family.
A separate checker reviews the exact implementation revision and preserves all passing and failing held-outs.
